summary: Backend only. Reviewed the background legacy migration code and tested it on throwaway DBs. Batch insert, conflict counting, idempotence, counters and docs without an id, and per-collection error isolation all work (12/12 checks). After a backend restart, 'Application startup complete' was logged before both legacy migrations finished. Both migrations inserted 0 records. test_database counts per company were the same before and after the restart for invoices, customers, payments, counters, stock, expenses, audit_log and attendance. Legacy DBs were unchanged.

minor.issue: Each restart logs 44 'prices' conflicts per company. The unique index on (company_id, zone, category, size) blocks the legacy rows because the main DB already has rows for the same key with different ids. I checked: all 45 Wholesale and 136 Manufacturing legacy price values match the main DB, so no data is lost. The warning repeats on every startup.

action_items: Optional: treat a conflict whose stored values match the legacy row as 'existing' (or check the unique key before inserting) so prices don't warn on every startup.

Production risk: target.distinct('id') returns one BSON document, limited to 16MB (roughly 300k+ uuid ids). A very large collection would fail on this call. The error is caught per collection, so that collection would never migrate. Consider an aggregation/cursor or a $in lookup per batch.

Production risk: pending holds all new docs of a collection in memory before batching. For a large attendance/audit_log this could cause OOM, which matches the pod dying during manufactoring.attendance. Consider flushing each 500-doc batch while iterating the cursor.
critical_code_review_comments: on_startup: the migration now runs via asyncio.create_task and does not block startup (confirmed in the logs). initialize_multi_company is wrapped in try/except OperationFailure. OK.

migrate_legacy_company_collection: insert_many(ordered=False) in batches of 500; 11000 errors are counted as conflicts and logged (first 5), other codes are re-raised; counters get the '<cid>:<_id>' _id. OK. A doc whose id is repeated inside the source is skipped as 'existing'.
There is no cross-process lock. If several workers or pods start at once, each one migrates, and collections without a unique id index could get duplicates. Low risk with a single uvicorn worker.
run_legacy_migration_in_background keeps no strong reference beyond the module global (OK) and logs the exception; the run retries on the next startup.
seed_data_creation: None. Used only the throwaway DBs tmp_mig_src, tmp_mig_tgt, tmp_mig_main and tmp_mig_main__*, all dropped afterwards.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run 'python tests/legacy_migration_batch_check.py' from /app/backend to check the migration on throwaway DBs. For a restart check, run 'legacy_migration_check.py snap /tmp/before.json', restart the backend, take the 'after' snapshot, then run 'diff' and 'verify'. The prices 'missing' entries are expected: matching rows exist with different ids.
